summary: A fractional CO2 laser used for skin texture, scarring and pore concerns.
leadAnswer: Resurfacing Laser at Kaiteki uses fractional CO2 laser technology to create controlled micro-injury columns in the skin, prompting a renewal response. It is commonly considered for texture, scarring and enlarged-pore concerns. It asks more of both recovery and skin type than the non-ablative lasers do, so a doctor is deliberate about who it is offered to.
seoDescription: Fractional CO2 resurfacing laser in Malaysia for skin texture, acne scarring and pores. Book a free consultation with a Kaiteki doctor to assess suitability.
typicalSessions: A small course, spaced weeks apart
bringToConsult: Raise any history of cold sores, or of scarring badly, without being asked: both change whether, and how, it is done.

avoidIf.body: in the area, including acne or cold sores.

avoidIf.lead: A history of keloid or hypertrophic scarring.
Recently tanned skin, or recent isotretinoin.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and recovery planning
sessionSteps.body: Your first visit is a consultation, not a treatment. For an ablative laser it includes planning your recovery around work or events before anything is booked.

sessionSteps.title: Numbing, then the laser
sessionSteps.body: Topical numbing is applied, then the laser is passed across the area at settings chosen for your skin.

sessionSteps.title: Healing between sessions
sessionSteps.body: Sessions are spaced several weeks to a few months apart, so the skin heals and remodels fully between visits.

afterSession.intro: Expect more downtime than with non-ablative lasers. Redness, swelling and flaking or peeling over several days to about a week are common and typically settle. Diligent sun protection and gentle skincare follow.

bands.title: The first day or two
bands.body: Treated skin looks red, feels hot and tight, and is visibly swollen.

bands.title: The rest of the week
bands.body: Bronzing, roughness and flaking as the treated columns work their way out. Pinkness can linger for weeks.

afterSession.aftercare: Gentle cleansing, the emollient you are given, no picking or exfoliating, and strict daily sun protection. Heat, swimming, makeup and active skincare are paused for as long as your doctor specifies.

risks.intro: Temporary effects include redness, swelling, peeling and changes in pigmentation. Because the laser is ablative, the skin is genuinely wounded and then heals, so infection and scarring are real if uncommon possibilities. That is why aftercare here is instruction rather than advice.
risks.common: Redness, swelling, heat, crusting and peeling, and pinkness that can last for weeks.
risks.lessCommon: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, prolonged redness, reactivation of cold sores, infection, and scarring or textural change.
risks.pigmentNote: Deeper and Asian skin tones carry a higher risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after ablative resurfacing, so settings are kept conservative, priming skincare may be advised, and more sessions at lower intensity may be preferred over one aggressive session.
cannotDo: It is not a lunchtime treatment: the recovery is real and has to be planned for.
Established acne scarring generally needs a course, not one visit.
It works on texture and structure, not on skin colour alone.
risks.disclose: Tell your doctor about any history of cold sores, scarring or pigment problems, and any recent isotretinoin.

costFactors.intro: Sessions and cost depend on the concern, the treatment depth and how your skin responds. Depth and density are set for your skin type, and they are what the cost tracks, so it is confirmed at consultation rather than published as a rate.
factors: The depth and density of settings your concern calls for.
How many sessions the plan involves.

sections.heading: What is Resurfacing Laser treatment?
body: Resurfacing Laser refers to ablative and fractional laser technology (at Kaiteki, a fractional CO2 laser) that works by creating a controlled pattern of micro-injury columns across the treated skin, leaving surrounding tissue intact to support recovery.

This differs from non-ablative lasers such as Pico laser, which do not remove tissue at the surface. It is commonly considered for acne scarring and uneven texture, enlarged pores, and fine lines or other textural irregularity.

sections.heading: Why does a fractional CO2 laser heal faster than full resurfacing?
body: The fractional CO2 laser delivers energy in a grid-like pattern of microscopic columns, each surrounded by untreated skin. This fractional approach is intended to prompt a controlled skin-renewal and collagen-remodelling response while allowing faster recovery than treating the entire surface at once.

faqs.q: How much downtime should I expect?
faqs.a: More than with non-ablative lasers. Redness, swelling and flaking over several days to about a week are common and typically settle; how much depends on the settings used.
Topical numbing is usually applied beforehand. Many people describe a warm or prickling sensation during treatment.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: It depends on the concern and the treatment depth. The doctor sets the number and spacing of sessions once your skin has been assessed.

faqs.q: Is CO2 laser safe for Asian skin?
faqs.a: It is used on Asian skin, but more conservatively, because deeper skin tones carry a higher risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after ablative resurfacing. That often means lower settings across more sessions, and strict sun protection afterwards.

faqs.q: What is the difference between fractional and fully ablative CO2 laser?
faqs.a: Fully ablative resurfacing treats the whole surface in one pass, with a long recovery. Fractional delivery leaves untreated skin between microscopic columns, so healing draws on that intact skin and recovery is shorter. The trade-off is less surface treated per session, which is why a course is usual.
